item.title: Equivariant cohomology of stacky Lie group actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work we introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie groupoids and differentiable stacks. For Lie groupoids equipped with a strict action of a Lie 2-group, we define the corresponding equivariant cohomology via the Borel model and establish its Morita invariance. We also construct a simplicial Cartan model and prove that, under standard compactness assumptions, it recovers the equivariant cohomology defined via the Borel model. In the framework of stacky Lie group actions, we show that if a connected and \'etale stacky Lie group acts on a differentiable stack admitting an equivariant atlas, then the stacky action admits a strict presentation by a Lie 2-group action. Furthermore, we prove that different choices of equivariant atlases yield equivariantly Morita equivalent presenting actions, giving rise to a well-defined notion of equivariant cohomology for differentiable stacks. As an application, we compute the equivariant cohomology of toric symplectic stacks.
item.dc:creator: Daniel L\'opez Garcia, Cristian Ortiz, Roberto Villaflor

item.title: Generalized Gelfand-Cetlin data and abelianization
item.description: arXiv:2610.05422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hamiltonian-geometric analogue of restricting a complex representation of a compact connected Lie group $G$ to a maximal torus $T\subset G$ is symplectic implosion, as developed by Guillemin-Jeffrey-Sjamaar. The first author and Weitsman studied the effect on this analogy of replacing $T$ with a Gelfand-Cetlin torus. In particular, they identified symplectic quotients by $G$ at generic levels in $\mathfrak{g}^*_{\mathrm{reg}}$ with symplectic quotients by a Gelfand-Cetlin torus. On the other hand, the applicability of this result is limited to Hamiltonian $G$-spaces whose moment images intersect $\mathfrak{g}^*_{\mathrm{reg}}$. The purpose of the present work is to remove that constraint altogether. We construct generalized Gelfand-Cetlin data for each orbit-type stratum $\Sigma\subset\mathfrak{g}^*$. Each datum determines a Gelfand-Cetlin torus and a Hamiltonian action of that torus on an open subset of every connected Hamiltonian $G$-space whose principal orbit-type stratum is $\Sigma$. Our generalized abelianization theorem gives canonical isomorphisms of stratified symplectic spaces between reductions by $G$ at generic levels in $\Sigma$ and corresponding reductions by the Gelfand-Cetlin torus. Using symplectic implosion, we extend the Gelfand-Cetlin abelianizations of the first author and Weitsman to non-regular elements of $\mathfrak{g}^*$. We subsequently illustrate this theorem by using the first author and Mayrand's theory of symplectic reduction along a submanifold to construct a canonical family of Hamiltonian $G$-spaces whose moment images lie entirely outside the regular locus. The positive-dimensional reductions of these spaces are realized as reductions by Gelfand-Cetlin tori.
item.dc:creator: Peter Crooks, Mitchell Pound

item.title: Mixed tori in contact surgery diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2510.19580v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a diagrammatic framework for applying the symplectic JSJ decomposition to exact/weak symplectic fillings of 3-dimensional contact manifolds. Namely, we apply the symplectic JSJ decomposition to a contact surgery diagram for some $(Y,\zeta)$, producing a finite collection of contact manifolds, also described diagrammatically, whose exact/weak symplectic fillings determine those of $(Y,\zeta)$. We apply this technique to recover known symplectic filling classifications for certain lens spaces and torus bundles, and also to provide an algorithm for classifying the exact/weak symplectic fillings of a large class of plumbed 3-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Austin Christian, Tanushree Shah

item.title: Proper kernels in microlocal sheaf theory
item.description: arXiv:2511.02677v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be real analytic manifolds and let $\Lambda \subseteq T^*X$ and $\Sigma \subseteq T^*Y$ be closed conic subanalytic singular isotropics. Given a sheaf $K \in \mathrm{Sh}_{-\Lambda \times \Sigma}(X \times Y)$ microsupported in $-\Lambda \times \Sigma$, consider the convolution functor $(-) \ast K \colon \mathrm{Sh}_{\Lambda}(X) \rightarrow \mathrm{Sh}_{\Sigma}(Y)$ from sheaves microsupported in $\Lambda$ to sheaves microsupported in $\Sigma$. We show that the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ preserves compact objects if and only if for each $x \in X$, the restriction $K|_{\{x\} \times Y} \in \mathrm{Sh}_\Sigma(Y)$ is a compact object. By a result of Kuo-Li, the functor sending a sheaf kernel $K$ to the convolution functor $(-) \ast K$ is an equivalence between the category $\mathrm{Sh}_{-\Lambda \times \Sigma}(X \times Y)$ of sheaves microsupported in $-\Lambda \times \Sigma$ and the category of cocontinuous functors from $\mathrm{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$ to $\mathrm{Sh}_\Sigma(Y)$. We therefore classify all cocontinuous functors that preserve compact objects between the two categories. Our approach is entirely categorical and requires minimal input from geometry: we introduce the notion of a proper object in a compactly generated stable infinity-category and study its properties under strongly continuous localizations to obtain the result. The main geometric input is the analysis of compact and proper objects of the category of $P$-constructible sheaves for a triangulation $P$ of a manifold $Z$ via the exit path category $\mathrm{Exit}(Z, P) \simeq P$. Along the way, we show that a sheaf $F \in \mathrm{Sh}_\Lambda(X)$ is proper if and only if it has perfect stalks, which is equivalent to a result of Nadler.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Hu
